name: bulletin-app
//: Build identity + manifest wiring for @skew/build.
prebuild  — `skew-build stamp` derives a buildId (git SHA + UTC timestamp,
e.g. 'a053212-20260810T143012Z') and writes it to
src/app/skew-build-id.generated.ts so the bundle knows its own
identity, and mirrors it into a <meta name="skew-build-id">
tag via the index HTML transform so the served index.html can
be identified without executing JS.
postbuild — `skew-build manifest` scans the built output and emits
skew-manifest.json ALONGSIDE index.html: { buildId, builtAt,
chunks: { <name>: <hashed filename> } }. The runtime fetches
it with cache:'no-store' to decide whether the origin has a
newer build than the bundle currently running.
Deploy/CDN rules that make the runtime checks trustworthy:
1. Upload order: hashed chunk files FIRST, then index.html and
skew-manifest.json together, LAST. The manifest must never claim a
build whose chunks aren't fully uploaded yet.
2. Cache headers: hashed chunks -> immutable, 1y.
index.html AND skew-manifest.json -> no-store (or max-age=0,
must-revalidate). The manifest is the staleness oracle; if a CDN
region caches it stale, it reports the OLD buildId and the runtime
correctly refuses to auto-reload there (banner instead of a loop) —
which is exactly the incident behavior we want.
3. Keep the previous deploy's chunks on the origin for a grace window
if you can; recovery then becomes a non-event for most users.

scripts.deploy: npm run build && npm run deploy:assets && npm run deploy:entry
scripts.deploy:assets: echo 'upload dist/**/*.{js,css,woff2,map} (hashed, immutable) to CDN first'
scripts.deploy:entry: echo 'then upload index.html + skew-manifest.json together, Cache-Control: no-store'
